did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah begins his complaint by acknowledging the Lord’s righteousness, yet asks why the way of the wicked prospers and why treacherous people live in peace.

Did you know? Jeremiah describes the wicked as those whom the Lord planted; they have even taken root and borne fruit. Yet their closeness to the Lord is only on their lips, while their hearts are far from him.

Did you know? The Lord’s answer to Jeremiah uses the image of a race: if running with men has worn him out, how will he compete with horses? This emphasizes that he must prepare for even greater difficulties.
Did you know? The Lord warns Jeremiah not to trust even his brothers and his own family, because they too have betrayed him and spoken kindly to him only outwardly.
Did you know? The Lord describes Israel’s abandonment in deeply painful terms: he has forsaken his house and abandoned his inheritance, giving his beloved people into the hands of their enemies.

Did you know? The Lord’s inheritance is compared to a bird of prey surrounded by other birds. As a result, the wild animals are called to gather and devour it—a vivid picture of the land being handed over to its enemies.
Did you know? The destruction is also portrayed through the image of a vineyard: many shepherds have ruined the vineyard, trampled its plot, and turned the precious land into a desolate wilderness.

Did you know? The chapter’s image of sowing and reaping highlights the consequences of sin: the people sowed wheat but harvested thorns, meaning that their labor and produce brought no benefit because of the Lord’s anger.

Did you know? The judgment is not directed only at Judah: the Lord declares that the neighboring nations that harmed Israel’s inheritance will also be uprooted from their land, and in the same context he says that the house of Judah will be uprooted from among them.

Did you know? The chapter leaves room for restoration even for the neighboring nations: if they learn the ways of the Lord’s people, swear by his name instead of by Baal, and follow his ways, they may be established among his people. But if they do not listen, they will be uprooted and destroyed.
